credit.name: Central Laboratory for Quality of Seeds and Planting Material

description: Single-file offline HTML application for quality-control review, control charting and audit of real-time PCR (qPCR) runs. It reads IXO, EDS/EDT, RDML, ZPCR and PCRD instrument files directly in a browser with no installation, server or network connection, checks each run against a stored laboratory SOP profile, charts instrument and assay parameters across runs, and exports figures, tables and a signed report with identifiers optionally pseudonymised.

documentation.note: Archived release carrying the citation and the declared licences.
Project wiki: command mode and voice commands, and the technical description of the build.

download.note: Mirror of the published single-file builds.
Repository holding the source and the build inputs.
The application: one self-contained HTML file. Save it and open it in a browser; it selects a modern runtime (Chrome, Edge) or an ECMAScript 5 compatibility runtime at load time.

function.cmd:
lab Laboratory of molecular biology
analyst A. Analyst
run all
only img:curves target=all signal=stored log=yes
select data:runs_and_qc run=all rows=200 pseudo=yes
zip handover
function.note: Assembles a selection of figures and tables into one quality-control report, written by a PDF writer inside the page with no external service. The cover states laboratory, analyst, SOP profile name and profile checksum, the files read and their checksums, and the contents. The archive form carries each figure as SVG together with the CSV behind it, tables as CSV, the selection list and the SOP profile, so every figure in a report can be traced back to its numbers. A forensic log records findings with severity, time, the object concerned and the evidence. Example only.

function.cmd:
run all
only img:curves target=all signal=stored log=yes
select img:stdcurve target=all
select img:repsd target=all
zip curves
function.note: Works on the amplification and melting data as recorded. Curves are shown on stored signal or on baseline-corrected signal, linear or log. Standard curves are fitted to give slope, intercept, r2 and amplification efficiency, with the factor taken as 10^(-1/slope) and efficiency as a percentage of it; log2 and log10 conventions are both reported against their ideal slopes. Replicate spread, endpoint fluorescence, amplitude, background and passive-reference level are derived per well. Stored threshold cycles are never overwritten: a recomputed value is displayed beside the stored one, and any difference is raised as a finding. Example only.

function.cmd:
run all
select cc:efficiency type=trend x=order
select cc:pc_cq type=i x=order
select cc:ntc_rate type=p x=order
select cc:ic_shift type=ewma x=order
zip assay_charts
function.note: Tracks assay and operator performance across runs: positive-control Cq and amplitude, passive-reference level and CV, amplification efficiency, no-template-control contamination rate, internal-control shift, replicate SD, late and low-confidence calls, row and column position effects, manual-edit rate, call-disagreement rate and copied results. Chart type is constrained per series and chosen from individuals, EWMA, CUSUM, trend, Xbar-S, p, u, c and funnel, parameterised by phase-1 length, lambda, L, k, h, specification limits and a warn-ahead horizon; a rate series takes p, a count series c, and an operator comparison funnel. Example only.

function.cmd:
run all
select cc:heat_rate type=trend x=order
select cc:lamp_drift type=i x=date
select cc:cycle_sd type=i x=order
select cc:log_errors type=c x=order
zip instrument_charts
function.note: Tracks instrument and software health across runs as statistical process-control charts: heating and cooling rate, overshoot, settling, transition, hold temperature, zone spread, heatsink and cover temperature; lamp reference and drift, LED current and junction temperature, exposure, saturation, calibration uniformity, background and ROI, filter-wheel timing and encoder; cycle-timing regularity, run duration, command response, late ticks, catch-up, image and ROI processing time, runtime errors and log errors. Charts are addressed as 'cc:<name>' and plotted against run order, date, instrument hours or cycles. Example only.

function.cmd:
run all
select data:cq_values run=all rows=200 pseudo=yes
select data:amplification_curves run=all rows=200 pseudo=yes
select data:melting_peaks run=all rows=200 pseudo=yes
zip export_tables
function.note: Writes the run out in formats other tools read, without altering stored values. Tables are addressed as 'data:<name>' and cover threshold cycles, amplification curves, melting peaks, multicomponent raw signal, plate map, run and QC summary, statistics, relative quantification, sample comparison, rising curves, experiment settings and metadata, SOP criteria and answers, control-chart series, instrument records and the forensic log. Options are run, rows and pseudo. 'pseudo=yes' substitutes pseudonyms for sample identifiers in everything written out; the mapping is not exported. Example only.

function.cmd:
run all
select data:experiment_meta run=all rows=200 pseudo=yes
select data:runs_and_qc run=all rows=200 pseudo=yes
zip intake
function.note: Decodes the vendor container and reports what was accepted or refused and why. IXO and RDML are XML; EDS, EDT, ZPCR and PCRD are compound or compressed containers, unpacked in the browser. Each file is checksummed, its internal structure checked for truncation and entry mismatch, and its decode time recorded, so a renamed, partial or tampered container is reported rather than silently half-read. Extracted per run: instrument and firmware identity, protocol and thermal programme, plate geometry, well roles, targets and dyes, acquisition points, and the run and edit timestamps. Example only.

function.cmd:
run all
select data:sop_criteria run=all rows=200 pseudo=yes
select data:sop_answers run=all rows=200 pseudo=yes
select img:outcomes target=all
zip sop_review
function.note: Evaluates each run against a stored laboratory SOP profile. The profile is a versioned document with its own name and SHA-256, covering control materials and their expected behaviour, acceptance criteria, outcome vocabulary and the rules that map evidence to a call. Every criterion is answered per run with the value it was judged on, so an acceptance decision can be reconstructed. Where a run carries a call made on the instrument, the stored call and the SOP outcome are compared and a disagreement is raised as a finding rather than resolved silently. Internal controls are evaluated as controls, not as assay targets. Example only.
